officials.name: Craig Robertson
officials.bio: Sheriff Craig A. Robertson was born in Frostburg, Maryland, and graduated from Allegany College of Maryland in Criminal Justice. A 30-year veteran of law enforcement, he was elected Sheriff in 2010 after serving in various roles with the Cumberland City Police and the Sheriff's Office. He is a graduate of the FBI National Academy on Leadership and Management.

officials.name: Julie Hummer
officials.bio: Julie Hummer represents District 4 in the western part of Anne Arundel County and resides in the Laurel portion of her district with her husband Jon and their 5 children. Julie is a strong advocate on issues of housing affordability, transportation, parks and recreation, and economic growth.

officials.name: Peter Smith
officials.bio: Pete Smith is a long-time advocate for District 1 who pledges to serve the residents with vigor and heart. He has two children and lives in Jessup. As a Major in the Marines, he is an Intelligence Officer and the regional coordinator for Toys for Tots in addition to serving on the board of several other community organizations.

officials.name: Allison M. Pickard
officials.bio: Allison Pickard represents District 2 and resides in the Millersville portion of her district with her husband and three children. Allison is a passionate advocate for revitalization, housing, equity, and environmental issues.

officials.name: Amanda Fiedler
officials.bio: As the representative for District 5, Amanda Fiedler strives to serve her constituents with deep compassion and care. Ms. Fielder is proud to call District 5 home and everyone who lives there a neighbor.

officials.name: Lisa D. B. Rodvien
officials.bio: Lisa Rodvien is proud and honored to represent Anne Arundel County's 6th District. During her time on the County Council, she has worked hard to pass laws that will protect our environment, strengthen our schools, and address our County's housing crisis.

officials.name: Nathan Volke
officials.bio: Nathan Volke represents District 3 and resides in Pasadena with his wife and two children. Nathan strives to bring transparency and financial responsibility, providing a connection between the constituents of District 3 and all county, state, federal & private agencies. He has proved his reputation as a vocal council member on protecting Anne Arundel County and District 3 from special interest groups and tax increases.

officials.name: Shannon Leadbetter
officials.bio: Shannon Leadbetter is honored to serve the residents of District 7 in Anne Arundel County as the District 7 Councilmember. She encourages residents to reach out to introduce themselves and their community.

officials.name: Everett Sesker
officials.bio: Sheriff Everett L. Sesker is a proud son of Anne Arundel County. He served 22 years with the Prince George's County Police Department, rising to the rank of Major, and later became Executive Director of the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission. Sworn in on December 6th, 2022, Sheriff Sesker is the first African American Sheriff for Anne Arundel County.

officials.name: Anne Colt Leitess
officials.bio: Anne Colt Leitess is the Elected State’s Attorney for Anne Arundel County since 2018, serving her second term. She began her career in Baltimore City in 1988 and later served as an Assistant State’s Attorney in Anne Arundel County from 1990-2013. A graduate of University of Baltimore Law School, she has focused most of her career on prosecuting homicides, violent crime, child homicide, and sexual assault cases.

officials.name: Dennis Brady
officials.bio: Councilman Brady was elected as an At-Large Councilman on November 7, 2023, having previously served on the City Council from 1994 to 2015. During his prior tenure, he was active in the Maryland Municipal League (MML) and the Prince George’s County Municipal Association (PGCMA), even serving as president for both organizations.

officials.name: Wanda Rogers
officials.bio: Wanda is the CEO of W Rogers Executive Consulting, LLC that she started in 2017. She is also the office manager for the family business, Realty Transaction Services. Wanda retired from the U.S. Department of the Treasury in 2017 after 36 years of federal service, where she held several high-ranking positions.

officials.name: Clinton Truesdale, Sr.
officials.bio: Clinton Boyce Truesdale has been a Prince George's County resident for over 40 years, residing in Bowie for 27 years. An entrepreneur and community activist, he was appointed to the Bowie City Council in February 2023 and re-elected in November 2023. He focuses on Economic Development, Public Safety, and Community Engagement, and serves as Council Liaison to the Advisory Planning Board and Community Recreation Committee.

officials.name: Roxy Ndebumadu
officials.bio: Roxy Ndebumadu is a two-term Bowie City Councilmember, geoeconomic strategist, and founder whose work bridges governance, technology, and economic opportunity. She brings a cross-sector perspective shaped by public service, global technology leadership, and civic institution-building. In 2019, she made history as the youngest woman elected to the Bowie City Council and the first African American woman to represent District 4 in the State of Maryland.

officials.name: Zipporah Miller
officials.bio: Councilmember Zipporah Miller was elected to fill the District 1 seat in June 2026. Councilmember Miller is Council Liaison to the following City committees: Arts Committee Community Outreach Committee.

officials.name: Dufour Woolfley
officials.office: Mayor Pro Tem, City Council Member
officials.bio: Dufour Woolfley was re-elected to the District 2 seat in November 2023 and selected as Mayor Pro Tem. He has served on the Council since March 2018, and previously in an At-Large term from January 2015. A Bowie resident for over 20 years, he has been active in city affairs and community advocacy, serving on various committees and boards.

officials.name: Michael Estève
officials.bio: Michael Estève is a lifelong Bowie resident. Raised by an Army Officer and English teacher, he is the product of Prince George's County public elementary and middle schools. He is a graduate of DeMatha Catholic High School and received a B.A. from Loyola University Maryland.

officials.name: Catherine M. Grasso
officials.bio: County Commissioner Catherine Grasso took office in December 2022, representing District 3 and working for all citizens of Calvert County on the Calvert County, Maryland, Board of County Commissioners. She is serving her first term. Before retiring from federal service, Grasso formulated and executed the budget for an agency of the U.S. Department of Agriculture.

officials.name: Earl F. "Buddy" Hance
officials.bio: County Commissioner Earl “Buddy” Hance took office in December 2018 as an at-large representative on the Calvert County, Maryland, Board of County Commissioners. He is serving his second term, which began in December 2022. Hance served as secretary of the Maryland Department of Agriculture in the cabinet of Gov. Martin O'Malley from May 2009 to January 2015, after serving as deputy secretary of the department since February 2007.

officials.name: Mark C. Cox, Sr.
officials.bio: County Commissioner Mark C. Cox Sr. took office in December 2022 as the District 2 representative on the Calvert County, Maryland, Board of County Commissioners. He is serving his first term. Cox has been a Calvert County small business owner for over 40 years.

officials.name: Mike Hart
officials.bio: County Commissioner Mike Hart took office in December 2014, representing District 1 on the Calvert County, Maryland, Board of County Commissioners, and is currently serving his third term. A businessman with over 30 years of experience, he owns and operates Patuxent Wine & Spirits and Barrel 9 in Lusby. Hart is an active supporter of many charitable and educational organizations in Calvert County.

officials.name: Todd Ireland
officials.bio: County Commissioner Todd Ireland took office in December 2022 as an at-large representative on the Calvert County, Maryland, Board of County Commissioners, serving his first term. He previously served as a Calvert County Sheriff’s Deputy for nearly 29 years, retiring as a captain in December 2021. A lifelong Calvert County resident, he resides on his family’s farm in Huntingtown.

officials.name: Valerie D. Hawkins
officials.address: 225 North Center St. Room 023 Westminster, MD 21157

officials.name: Al Miller
officials.bio: Al Miller was elected to his first term of the Cecil County Council in 2018, and a second term in 2022; representing District Three, which includes Rising Sun, Cherry Hill, Calvert and Fair Hill. Mr. Miller graduated from the University of Delaware and has been in the agriculture profession for many years. He is currently working at Ag Industrial, Inc. selling New Holland Agriculture and Construction Equipment in Rising Sun.

officials.name: Bob Meffley
officials.bio: Bob Meffley was elected in 2016 as Council Member for the First District and appointed Council Vice President in 2022. A lifelong resident of Cecil County, he is a businessman who has owned and operated H&B Plumbing and Heating for 44 years.

officials.name: Dawn Branch
officials.bio: Dawn Branch, elected Council Member for District 5 in 2024, holds a Master of Science in Education and a Bachelor of Science in Business. She previously served two terms on the Cecil County School Board and is currently a Grant Assistant for Cecil County Public Schools. Committed to her community, she focuses on restoring checks and balances, prioritizing services, and enhancing quality of life in Cecil County.

officials.name: Donna Culberson
officials.bio: Donna Culberson was appointed to serve as the Council Member from the Fourth District, in 2022 which includes Perryville, Port Deposit, Charlestown, Colora, Bainbridge and Conowingo. Ms. Culberson attended Cecil College focusing on accounting and finance. She has been employed for the past 38 years in long term care healthcare.

officials.name: Rebecca Hamilton
officials.bio: Rebecca Hamilton was elected in 2022 to serve as the Council member from the Second District, representing Elkton, Elk Mills and Childs. Ms. Hamilton is a graduate of Goldey-Beacom College and holds an MBA from the University of Delaware. She has spent her career in the building materials industry in Sales Operations and plans to bring the same determination and resolve that she demonstrates each day to her role as Councilwoman.

officials.name: César Díaz
officials.bio: César Díaz moved to Frederick in 1997 and is an information technology professional who has worked with government agencies, international companies, and nonprofit organizations. He is the first Latino elected to the Frederick City Council and is a member of the Democratic Socialists of America, the RISE Coalition of Western Maryland, and the Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Frederick.

officials.name: Derek Shackelford
officials.bio: Council Member Dr. Derek Shackelford is honored to serve the residents of the City of Frederick. He values the privilege of collaborating, leading, and partnering with the community to ensure that Frederick remains a vibrant city where every resident has the opportunity to thrive. He looks forward to continuing his service.

officials.name: Joe Adkins
officials.bio: Joe Adkins serves as the City Council Member for District 4. He is focused on maintaining strong core services, supporting responsible budgeting, and protecting the character of Frederick’s neighborhoods. Joe is a member of the Evangelical Reformed United Church of Christ and serves on the C&O Canal National Park Advisory Commission.

officials.name: Katie Nash
officials.bio: Katie Nash serves as City Council Vice President and represents District 1, committed to preserving Frederick's unique character and celebrating its diversity. A graduate of Hood College, she has worked across various sectors and shares a blended family with her husband and three teenagers.

officials.name: Libby Taylor
officials.bio: Libby Taylor serves as an At-Large City Council Member and is passionate about improving quality of life for current and future residents of Frederick. As a policy analyst by profession, she places strong importance on effective policy implementation and evaluation to ensure City initiatives deliver meaningful results for the community.

officials.name: Peter Brehm
officials.bio: Peter is passionate about assuring that Frederick is a desirable and sustainable place to live, work, shop, and play. Peter is involved in Evangelical Reformed United Church of Christ, The Frederick Center, and PFLAG Frederick.

officials.name: Sarah Hempel Irani
officials.bio: Sarah Hempel Irani is passionate about pedestrian safety, neighborhood connectivity, the role of the built environment in shaping our lives, and meaningful civic engagement. She values collaboration and community-centered solutions that help Frederick thrive. Sarah is a member of Good Shepherd Lutheran Church, where she has been involved for more than 20 years. She is a member and former board member of the Association of Consultants for Liturgical Space and is part of the Blue Elephant Art Studios on West 5th Street. A professional sculptor, Sarah is best known for creating the Claire McCardell monument. She holds a master’s degree in Medieval and Renaissance Studies from Hood College and has taught sculpture at Frederick Community College.

officials.name: Michael O'Connor
officials.bio: Mayor Michael O’Connor is a lifelong Frederick resident with a background in local media, community service, and public leadership. He was first elected to the Board of Aldermen in 2009 and became Mayor in 2017.

He is honored to serve as Councilman and is looking forward to following in the steps of prior leaders by continuing their fine legacy of leadership. His focus is to enhance education, assure public and personal safety, and champion community vibrancy.

officials.name: Christopher M. Corchiarino
officials.bio: Christopher M. Corchiarino was elected November 8, 2022, and is serving his second term as a Queen Anne’s County Commissioner representing District 4. A 1992 graduate of Queen Anne's County High School, he earned a BA from the University of Maryland and a Juris Doctorate from the University of Baltimore School of Law, and is licensed to practice law in multiple states. He lives in Stevensville with his wife and three daughters, and has always sought ways to give back to the County.

officials.name: J. Patrick McLaughlin
officials.bio: Patrick McLaughlin was elected November 8, 2022, and is serving his first term as a Queen Anne’s County Commissioner representing District 2. He graduated from Drexel University with a bachelor’s degree in Business Administration and founded his own Specialty Medical Distribution company. After retiring from the medical field, he became the Owner/Operator of a local Allstate Insurance Agency and serves on several boards and commissions.

officials.name: Jack N. Wilson, Jr.
officials.bio: Jack N. Wilson, Jr. was re-elected November 8, 2022, serving his third term as a Queen Anne’s County Commissioner representing District 1. He was first appointed in 2015 and focuses on expanding trade programs in schools and broadband throughout the County. He graduated from Severna Park High School and completed a Steamfitters Apprenticeship Program.

officials.name: James J. Moran
officials.bio: James J. Moran was first appointed to the Queen Anne's County Commissioners in 2013 and was re-elected in 2022, now serving his third term as an At-Large Commissioner. A Marine Corps veteran, he founded his own construction businesses before entering public service. He is dedicated to preserving farmland and supporting the Drug Free Coalition in Queen Anne's County.

officials.name: Philip L. Dumenil
officials.bio: PHILIP L. DUMENIL was elected in November 8, 2022 and is serving his third, non-consecutive, term as a Queen Anne’s County Commissioner representing District 3. He was duly sworn and qualified as a Queen Anne's County Commissioner on Tuesday, December 6, 2022.

officials.name: Adam Van Grack
officials.address: Mayor and Council Chambers Rockville City Hall 111 Maryland Ave. Rockville, MD 20850
officials.bio: Adam Van Grack is a councilmember for the City of Rockville. He is liaison to the Environment Commission, Recreation and Park Advisory Board, and Rockville Sister Cities Corporation. He also serves as Rockville’s representative to the Metropolitan Washington Council of Government’s Chesapeake Bay and Water Resources Policy Committee and is co-chair of the Bar Association of Montgomery County Legal Ethics Committee.

officials.name: Barry Jackson
officials.address: Mayor and Council Chambers Rockville City Hall 111 Maryland Ave. Rockville, MD 20850
officials.bio: Barry Jackson is a councilmember in the City of Rockville. He is a liaison to the Commission on Aging, the Financial Advisory Board and a voting member of the Retirement Board.

officials.name: David Myles
officials.address: Mayor and Council Chambers Rockville City Hall 111 Maryland Ave. Rockville, MD 20850
officials.bio: David Myles, first elected in 2019 and re-elected in 2023, is serving his second term as a Rockville councilmember. He completed his pediatrics medical training in Baltimore, at Johns Hopkins Hospital. Myles first moved to Maryland in 2010, following medical and graduate school at Yale University, and is a proud Morehouse College alumnus.

officials.name: Izola (Zola) Shaw
officials.address: Mayor and Council Chambers Rockville City Hall 111 Maryland Ave. Rockville, MD 20850
officials.bio: Izola (Zola) Shaw is a councilmember for the City of Rockville. She is liaison to the Human Rights Commission, Rockville Housing Enterprises and the Metropolitan Washington Council of Governments’ Region Forward Coalition. Shaw has served on several Montgomery County and city boards and committees, including the Charter Review Commission.

officials.name: Kate Fulton
officials.address: Mayor and Council Chambers Rockville City Hall 111 Maryland Ave. Rockville, MD 20850
officials.bio: Kate Fulton was elected in November 2023 and is serving her first term as a Rockville councilmember. She has over 20 years of professional experience making government work efficiently and effectively, having served in various roles at four federal agencies including senior counsel, chief of staff, and chief operating officer.

officials.name: Marissa Valeri
officials.address: Mayor and Council Chambers Rockville City Hall 111 Maryland Ave. Rockville, MD 20850
officials.bio: Councilmember Marissa Valeri was born and raised in Wheaton, Montgomery County, and has lived in Rockville for 13 years. She graduated from the University of Maryland Global Campus and has 27 years of professional experience in the nonprofit sector, focusing on health-care access and physician membership associations.

officials.name: Monique Ashton
officials.address: Mayor and Council Chambers Rockville City Hall 111 Maryland Ave. Rockville, MD 20850
officials.bio: Monique Ashton is mayor of the City of Rockville and is the first mayor of color in the city’s history. She is also president of the Montgomery Chapter of the Maryland Municipal League and District 5 vice president at the state level.
